Marathon Petroleum stock fell 5.3% today after surging nearly 7% over the prior three trading days. The sharp reversal follows Treasury Secretary Bessent's announcement on September 22nd that all Iranian airlines will be shut down starting Wednesday—a dramatic escalation in U.S.-Iran tensions that initially pushed oil prices higher on Monday and Tuesday (crude rose amid geopolitical concerns). However, the stock's decline today suggests the market is now pricing in the risk that heightened sanctions and international tensions could disrupt global oil supply chains in ways that hurt refiner margins, or that further diplomatic pressure could provoke a broader regional conflict that destabilizes energy markets unpredictably.

The volatility reflects the inherent tension in refining stocks during geopolitical shocks: while higher oil prices can boost refiners' input costs, the real driver of profits is the "crack spread"—the gap between what they sell refined products for and what crude costs them. With the Saudi East-West pipeline already shut down and Asian demand potentially tightening, uncertainty about which way crude supplies and product demand will move has likely made investors nervous about locking in positions ahead of unclear policy developments.
